subject: Nanotechnology
title: DNA Tiles and Bricks
description: Learn DNA Tiles and Bricks in one minute.

hook.text: What if you skip the scaffold entirely? DNA bricks are short strands that snap together like molecular LEGO.

buildup.text: Each 32-nucleotide brick has four binding domains — it connects to four neighbors in a 3D lattice, no scaffold needed.

discovery.text: From a master library of 1000 bricks, you select subsets to build any desired 3D shape — omit bricks to carve voids.

twist.text: DNA bricks need hundreds of unique strands for one shape — cost and yield remain practical barriers to scaling.

climax.text: Yin's lab built a 3D teddy bear from DNA bricks — demonstrating that modular DNA can rival origami in complexity.

punchline.text: Skip the scaffold, use bricks — DNA LEGO builds anything at the nanoscale.

quiz.question: How do DNA bricks differ from DNA origami?
options: DNA bricks use a long scaffold strand while origami does not
DNA bricks are short modular strands that connect without a scaffold, like LEGO pieces
DNA bricks can only form flat 2D structures
